tweets: Four temples, scattered at the four edges of a subcontinent, were stitched into ONE pilgrimage so that walking all of them means walking the whole land. 🙏

Badrinath sits near 10,000 ft in the Himalayas, where the Mahabharata says the sages Nara and Narayana once meditated. Dwarka rises on Gujarat's western coast, revered by tradition as Krishna's legendary capital.

On the east, Puri's Jagannath Temple (built in the 12th century CE) hosts the great Ratha Yatra chariot procession. On the south, Rameswaram's Ramanathaswamy Temple marks where the Ramayana says Rama worshipped Shiva before crossing to Lanka.

Tradition credits the 8th-century philosopher Adi Shankaracharya with linking these four — north, west, east, south — into a single circuit, each paired with a monastic seat (matha), weaving local shrines into one shared map of the sacred land.

Four directions, four epics, one pilgrimage. The Char Dham turns geography itself into scripture. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history. 🇮🇳
